title: Pointer rays and plane dragging
purpose: Turn pointer positions into world rays for perspective and orthographic three.js cameras, intersect rays with planes, and drag objects across a plane keeping the grab offset, with optional grid snapping laid in the plane. Use it for editors, board games and placement tools.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: No three.js needed: pass camera.projectionMatrixInverse.elements and camera.matrixWorld.elements. The demo was rendered with three.js 0.186.1 in headless Chrome.

exports.name: ndcFromPointer
exports.summary: Normalized device coordinates from a pointer over an element's bounding rectangle; +y up.

exports.name: rayFromCamera
exports.signature: rayFromCamera(ndcX, ndcY, inverseProjection, cameraWorld, nearDepth = -1) -> {origin, direction}
exports.summary: The world ray under a point, origin on the near plane, unit direction; perspective or orthographic.

exports.name: intersectRayPlane
exports.signature: intersectRayPlane(origin, direction, normal, constant) -> t | null
exports.summary: Distance along the ray to normal . p + constant = 0, or null when parallel or behind.

exports.name: planeFromNormalAndPoint
exports.summary: The plane through a point, with a unit normal.

exports.name: invertMatrix
exports.summary: Inverse of a column-major 4 x 4 matrix; singular throws RangeError.

exports.name: PlaneDrag
exports.signature: new PlaneDrag(options); begin(ray, objectPosition) -> boolean; move(ray) -> [x, y, z] | null; end(); hit(ray); snapToGrid(position); active
exports.summary: Drag controller that keeps the grab offset and snaps to a grid in the plane.

exports.name: PLANE_DRAG_DEFAULTS
exports.summary: Frozen default options: normal, constant, snap.

options.name: constant
options.meaning: Plane constant in normal . p + constant = 0.

options.name: snap
options.meaning: Grid step in the plane; 0 for no snapping.

limits: Planes only: no dragging along a surface, an axis gizmo or a sphere. A drag whose ray runs parallel to the plane or points away from it returns null, so very flat camera angles over a ground plane lose the drag until the pointer comes back. Snapping rounds in the plane's own two-axis grid, which for tilted planes is not the world grid. Rays start on the near plane; for a WebGPU projection pass nearDepth 0. No pointer capture or event wiring is included. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run for the demo, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Unprojecting clip-space points through the inverse projection and camera world matrices
Ray and plane intersection t = -(n . o + c) / (n . d)
Grid snapping in an orthonormal basis of the plane
